content:
The formal team (@Simon Sorg @Jason Rute @Mert Ünsal @Indraneel Mukherjee @Roman Soletskyi ) at Mistral is excited to share what we have been building for the last couple of months: We’re open-sourcing Leanstral today (blogpost, hf weights) It is the first fully open-source code agent built for Lean.

The Leanstral model is a highly efficient architecture with 6B active parameters, explicitly trained to operate inside real formal repositories. On our new FLTEval benchmark, it outperforms open-source alternatives 10 times larger like the latest QWen3.5, Kimi K2.5, and GLM5. Use it through Mistral Vibe for free.

Some remarks:

  • You are responsible for your code. Don’t commit AI slop to Mathlib as maintainers are already overwhelmed.

  • With a tiny model that is 90x cheaper, we are behind closed-source SoTA Claude Opus in terms of performance. We intend to keep the cost of using Leanstral low for the community (therefore released with a Mistral Labs experimental endpoint).

  • Take it for a spin. Break it. Tell us where it fails so we can build an open model that does beat Opus.

Discussion thread: #Model comparisons for Lean > Leanstral Discussion.

[Update] Here is a quick start guide for getting started with Leanstral.

Installing Mistral Vibe and Leanstral

  • Install Mistral vibe at https://console.mistral.ai/codestral/cli
    • Make an account
    • Select the free plan. (No need to use Mistral Pro to use Leanstral.)
    • Make an API key.
  • Go to https://admin.mistral.ai/plateforme/privacy and opt into the Mistral Labs privacy settings.
  • Use the commands from https://console.mistral.ai/codestral/cli in your terminal to install Mistral Vibe.
  • Setup should happen automatically, requesting your API key. But if not, use vibe --setup from the terminal.
  • In vibe type /leanstall (lean + [in]stall).
  • Shift-tab multiple times until leanstral displays at the top.

Using Leanstral

  • Type vibe --agent lean in the terminal (ensure leanstral displays at the top).
    • Recommend running vibe inside vs code terminal so you can see both vibe and your code.
    • Recommend running vibe inside your Lean project directory.

Example Prompts (these are just examples, try your own prompts!):

  • "Explain this project to me"
  • "Fill in the sorry in <some theorem in your project>"
  • "Make a new file with a proof that <insert your favorite math fact>"
  • "I'm stuck at the proof of <some theorem in your project>. I'm looking for a theorem like ... to finish the theorem. Is there anything like this in Mathlib?"
  • "Formalize the theorem from the paper located in ..."
  • "Break up the theorem <some theorem in your project> into lemmas."
  • "Golf the proof of <some theorem in your project> to be shorter"
  • "Rename ... to ... throughout the whole project"
  • "Upgrade the project to use the newest stable version of Lean"

Important:

  • The system is interactive. If it doesn't do what you want, correct it and tell it what you want it to do. Have a conversation with Leanstral.
